newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Boots confident of BHI payback.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Boots confident of BHI payback.

text.p: Britain's biggest chemist Boots Co Plc said on Thursday it would keep up investment in its over-the-counter healthcare business, confident it can create value over time.
Deputy chairman and chief executive Lord Blyth said Boots was not too worried about Boots Healthcare International making a profit at this stage as the emphasis focused on developing the business.
"Frankly we're not concerned about it making a bottom line profit at this point in time," he said in a telephone interview. "We're concerned about growing it as rapidly as we possibly can."

BHI, which develops and markets over-the-counter medicines, is in the process of launching products such as Nurofen pain relief across Europe. Last year Boots invested about 85 million stg in the business and expects to spend another 95 million in the current year.
"As long as we can work out that that business has the capacity to create value over time, making a short term profit isn't a great consideration for us," Blyth said.
But he said on the other hand the business was likely to break into the black in the next couple of years.
Boots, which earlier reported an 8.7 percent increase in annual profits, said BHI made a loss before exceptionals of 6.6 million stg, against a loss of 8.2 million in the previous year.
Boots also announced a 400 million stg cash payout to investors via a special dividend with its results, leaving Boots with net debt on its balance sheet.
Blyth said Boots was ready to give more surplus cash to shareholders in the future unless the company were to make very significant acuqisitiions.
"We are very cash generative...our shareholders have a very clear understanding from us that if we can't think of anything better to do with it we will give the cash back to them," he said.
Blyth said Boots had also been investing in its businesses, including nearly 100 million stg on BHI, 170 million on acquisitions last year and plus expansion of Boots The Chemist and Halfords.

But he said because of Boots' cash generative qualities there would always be situations where the group had surplus cash. "And having a non-debt balance sheet is not a very tax efficient thing to do," the chief executive said.
Blyth said Boots' home improvement business Do It All should be cash positive in the current year, after reducing its losses last year by two-thirds.
Blyth said the company would "wait and see" on where it took the business from here on.
He said the DIY market had proven much less attractive in overall terms and market leader B&Q had become more powerful. "It's been a much tougher situation than we expected."

Boots share of Do It All's losses last year was 6.9 million stg, against 10.1 million a year ago. Last year Boots became sole owner of the chain when it bought out joint venture partner W.H. Smith Group Plc. --Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
